true_cost_of_2bit.vs_unadapted_fp16_raw: 26.9519 / 21.3708 = 1.26x worse (MISLEADING -- flattered by the QAT model's domain adaptation)

analysis.size_caveat: The QAT Q2_K file is 495 MB vs PTQ's 347 MB (+43%), because 9 skip-layers and the embeddings stay F16. This is NOT an iso-size comparison, so the README's 'same 2-bit size and speed' framing does not hold for these two artifacts.
analysis.leakage_check: qat/data.py load_wikitext2_train_examples uses split='train'; the eval corpus is split='test'. No train/eval overlap.

these_numbers_overstate_generality_see_c.note: IMPORTANT when quoting anything in this file. The QAT models train on a WikiText-2 TRAIN blend and are scored on WikiText-2 TEST -- no leakage, but the domains match, so these scores partly measure domain alignment. results/c4_perplexity.json re-runs four of these checkpoints on an off-domain C4 slice.
these_numbers_overstate_generality_see_c.what_changes: The blend-vs-Alpaca-only spread collapses from 2.63x here (26.95 vs 70.88) to 1.31x on C4 (55.95 vs 73.03), and the best QAT model goes from 1.26x worse than fp16 here to 1.90x worse on C4. Roughly half the blend's apparent advantage is domain alignment.
these_numbers_overstate_generality_see_c.what_holds: QAT still beats PTQ by 6.46x on C4, so the central 2-bit QAT-vs-PTQ claim survives off-domain.

bit_annealing_is_a_noop.note: CONFIRMED by the qat_q2k_affine_noanneal control run: the progressive 4->2 bit-annealing schedule makes no significant difference at 1000 steps.
bit_annealing_is_a_noop.verdict: Statistically a no-op. The confidence intervals [26.732, 27.171] and [26.686, 27.124] overlap across almost their entire width, and the gap (0.047) is roughly a fifth of a single run's stderr. Disabling annealing is free. This matters methodologically: the SEQ runs also disable annealing, so without this control their difference from the headline run would have confounded two changes at once.

seq_evaluation.note: ParetoQ SEQ (--quant-function seq) evaluated against affine at matched settings (both fixed 2-bit, so the quant function is the only difference).
seq_evaluation.verdict: NOT a demonstrated win. SEQ is nominally 0.31 better, but the CIs overlap ([26.378, 26.810] vs [26.686, 27.124]). Note also that llama-perplexity's stderr is a within-run estimate over chunks; it does not capture seed-to-seed variance between two separate training runs, so the true uncertainty on this comparison is wider than the intervals suggest. Read this as a tie. The paper's claimed 2-bit advantage over LSQ-style quantization is neither reproduced nor refuted here.
seq_evaluation.init_sensitivity_is_the_real_finding: SEQ is extremely sensitive to shadow-weight init: 39.67 with ptq_q2k vs 26.594 with roundtrip, a 1.49x swing from the init mode alone, with everything else identical. An earlier reading of the ptq_q2k number alone suggested 'SEQ is 1.47x worse than affine'; that conclusion was an artifact of the init pairing, not a property of SEQ. ParetoQ initializes from fp weights, which roundtrip approximates and ptq_q2k does not.
seq_evaluation.export_penalty_is_not_differential: SEQ's Q2_K round-trip error on a sampled tensor is higher than affine's (3.03% vs 1.46%), but end-to-end the proxy->GGUF degradation is nearly identical (SEQ 29.85->39.67 = 1.33x; affine 19.64->26.91 = 1.37x). The export path does not penalize SEQ disproportionately.

wasserstein_evaluation.note: Sliced-Wasserstein + MSE hidden-state block alignment (arXiv:2601.07878, --distill-loss wasserstein) evaluated against CAKLD as the distillation objective. CLOSED: neither the initial run nor the scale-matched sweep beat CAKLD, and no further variations will be run on this project.
wasserstein_evaluation.verdict: CAKLD wins. Best Wasserstein result is 27.4029 (distill-weight 0.05) vs CAKLD's 26.9519. The intervals [27.179, 27.627] and [26.732, 27.171] do not overlap, though only barely -- they are adjacent. So this is a real but small loss, not a rout.
wasserstein_evaluation.monotone_trend: Quality degrades monotonically as the Wasserstein weight rises (27.40 -> 28.05 -> 30.71). The best tested weight is the smallest one, so within the range tested the term is a net negative at every setting. CAUTION: a distill-weight 0 point was NOT run, so this does not establish that the optimum is at zero -- only that quality is decreasing in weight across the three points measured.

weight_scale_confound.why_the_first_run_was_not_a_fair_test: The first Wasserstein run reused CAKLD's --distill-weight 0.5. That looks like a controlled swap but is not: the Wasserstein term is an unnormalized hidden-state MSE whose natural magnitude (kd_loss ~19-23) is an order of magnitude larger than CAKLD's KL-in-nats (kd_loss ~0.8-1.9). At the same nominal weight it therefore took 69-74% of the total loss where CAKLD takes 10-20% -- roughly a 5x shift in the task/distillation balance. That run measured 'Wasserstein-dominated training vs CAKLD-as-mild-regularizer', not the two objectives head to head.
weight_scale_confound.how_it_was_resolved: Re-ran at distill-weight 0.05 and 0.1, which bring the Wasserstein share to 13% and 31% -- 0.05 lands inside CAKLD's 10-20% band. With the scale matched, Wasserstein still loses, so the negative result is not an artifact of the weight.
weight_scale_confound.generalizable_lesson: --distill-weight is NOT comparable across --distill-loss choices. Any future distillation objective added to this repo needs its loss share checked against CAKLD's 10-20% before its weight is treated as equivalent.

wasserstein_evaluation.export_penalty_is_not_differential: proxy -> GGUF degradation is 1.42x for Wasserstein dw=0.5 and 1.37x for CAKLD, so the export path does not disadvantage Wasserstein; its deficit is already present in training.
wasserstein_evaluation.run_health: All four Wasserstein runs (100-step crash-check plus three 1000-step runs) completed with zero non-finite loss/gradient events and zero skipped updates. kd_loss started well above zero (22.95) and fell monotonically (to 9.14), confirming the student was genuinely quantized and the objective was actually optimizing. Gradient norms at dw=0.5 were high (157 falling to 29, vs ~10-50 for CAKLD), consistent with the loss-scale imbalance; they normalized at the lower weights.

seq_alpha_positivity_bug.note: Found while verifying SEQ's learnable alpha actually trains. Fixed in commit 6cd451e.
seq_alpha_positivity_bug.observed: After 1000 steps, 3 of 26,279,936 alpha scales had gone non-positive (min -3.0e-05). The count did not grow between step 100 and step 1000, and no run produced a NaN.
seq_alpha_positivity_bug.why_it_matters: alpha < 0 silently mirrors a group's quantization grid; alpha == 0 makes the backward's W_Q/alpha term 0/0 = NaN, which the |u| < 1 indicator cannot mask because nan * 0 == nan.
seq_alpha_positivity_bug.fix: abs().clamp_min(_EPS) on alpha in seq_fake_quant -- an exact identity for every alpha > _EPS, so all measured SEQ results above remain reproducible from the fixed code (verified bit-identical forward for positive alpha).
seq_alpha_positivity_bug.alpha_does_train: All 187 alpha tensors moved; mean relative change 0.14% at 100 steps growing to larger movement by 1000 (largest mover layers.16.mlp.up_proj at 2.02%). Not stuck at init.

batch24_fineweb_scaleup.note: Full-scale run (48828 steps, ~600M tokens, batch 24, lr 2.5e-5) testing whether reducing WikiText-2's share of the training blend (0.5 -> 0.05) and adding general-domain FineWeb data (0.5 share, see qat/data.py module docstring for why FineWeb over RedPajama/SlimPajama) generalizes better than the prior WikiText-heavy recipe -- motivated by the prior recipe's ~119x repetition of the 2.5M-token WikiText-2 train corpus at this token budget being a real memorization risk.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.result: Both eval sets improved sharply over the prior best (qat_q2k_blend): WikiText2 26.9519 -> 18.4863 (-31.4% relative), C4 55.9509 -> 32.2462 (-42.4% relative). The C4 (held-out, non-domain-matched) improvement is LARGER than the WikiText2 one, which is the result this run was actually testing for: the gain is not just domain-alignment inflation, it reflects genuine generalization improvement from the more diverse data mix.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.training_time_proxy_trough_caveat: The in-training (truncated, 20k-token) WikiText2 ppl proxy bottomed at step ~19,200 (~13.07) then drifted upward to 14.30 by the final step 48828 -- a real, gradual drift, not noise, plausibly from the ~12-13x repetition of this run's own (much smaller than before, but still finite) data pool late in training. The step-20,000 safety-net checkpoint, which would have let us test whether that trough held up under the REAL llama-perplexity/GGUF measurement, was UNRECOVERABLE: every train_qat.py --save-every checkpoint before this run's fix (see git log, 'Fix safety-net checkpoint overwrite') wrote to the same fixed filename, so each save silently overwrote the last, leaving only the step-47500 save by the time training finished.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.step47500_vs_final_result: Measured step 47500 anyway (the only other checkpoint that survived) against both eval sets as the closest available substitute: WikiText2 18.6311 +/- 0.1531 and C4 32.4342 +/- 0.2859, both statistically indistinguishable from the final checkpoint's 18.4863 +/- 0.1512 / 32.2462 +/- 0.2837 (overlapping stderr intervals). So on the REAL measurement, the late-training drift visible in the training-time proxy did NOT show up as a meaningful difference between these two nearby (1328-step-apart) points -- both are dramatically better than the prior recipe regardless. Whether the TRUE step-19,200 trough would have measured even better than either is now unknowable for this run; the checkpoint-overwrite bug is fixed for future ones.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.conclusion: Promote qat_q2k_fineweb_final as the new CURRENT BEST on both WikiText2 and C4, replacing qat_q2k_blend. No real basis to prefer the step-47500 checkpoint over it. NOTE: no 'beats fp16' claim is made anywhere in this result -- see results/c4_perplexity.json's analysis.batch24_fineweb_scaleup.fp16_ceiling_not_yet_run for why, and .fineweb_c4_overlap_validated for the FineWeb/C4 content-overlap check that was run before this result was trusted.
